procedural_matters: The panel of the international jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
facts: It was approximately 25 knots of wind.
FRA 95 was sailing upwind close-hauled on port tack, unable to bear away to gybe to go to the leeward gate.
JPN 310 was sailing upwind close-hauled on starboard tack, unable to bear away to gybe to go to the leeward gate.
FRA 95 passed head to wind in front of JPN 310 and tacked to starboard. At this point, JPN 310 was two boat lengths away.
JPN 310 tried to bear away to avoid FRA 95.
FRA 95 capsized to leeward on completion of her tack.
JPN 310 was unable to bear away due to the conditions, hardened up and sailed in between the boom and the hull of FRA 95.
The crew of FRA 95 extended his foot in order to prevent a collision between the two boats.
The collision caused damage to the rigging of FRA 95 and broke her tiller extension.
The collision caused injury to the FRA 95's crew's foot and she was unable to continue racing.
conclusions: It was not possible for JPN 310 to avoid FRA 95 in the conditions and she did not break rules 14 or 22.
